mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C300 petrol typically costs between £600 and £5,500 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M272 units start from £600-£1,500, reconditioned from £1,800-£3,200, and fully rebuilt M254 engines from £3,200-£5,500. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M272, M276, M274 and M254 engines in the C300 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M272 is a 3.0-litre naturally aspirated V6 used in the W204 C300 (2007-2012), producing 231 hp. The M276 is a 3.5-litre V6 used in the W204 facelift C300 (2012-2014), producing 252 hp. The M274 is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder used in the W205 C300 (2014-2021), producing 241-245 hp. The M254 is a 2.0-litre mild hybrid turbo used in the W206 C300 (2021-present), producing 258 hp.

mainEntity.name: What is the balance shaft failure on the M272 V6 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early M272 engines (2004-2008) suffer from balance shaft sprocket wear due to improperly hardened metal gears. This causes the timing to be thrown off, triggering fault codes P0016/P0017. Symptoms include a check engine light, rough idle, and potential engine damage if not addressed. Repair costs at a specialist are approximately £2,200-£3,500 for balance shaft and timing chain replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the M274 wrist pin issue and does it affect the C300?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M274 engine suffers from a wrist pin / piston seizure failure. Mercedes technical service bulletin LI03.10-P-060916 addresses the wrist pin concern. The knocking noise might be attributed to the unfavourable tolerance of the piston wrist pin resulting in enlarged end float of the connecting rod in the piston. A petition was submitted to NHTSA requesting an investigation into alleged 'wrong-sized wrist pins' in M274-equipped vehicles. There is no preventative fix - the first warning is often unusual engine noise or a misfire code.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 300 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All C300 petrol engines use timing chains, not belts. The M272 (W204), M276 (W204 facelift), M274 (W205) and M254 (W206) all use timing chains. However, the M272 is known for balance shaft sprocket wear affecting timing accuracy, and the M276 is known for camshaft adjuster rattle. A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign for timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300 petrol to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C300 petrol depends on the engine. On M272 engines, balance shaft sprocket wear can cause timing drift and power loss. On M274 engines, the wrist pin/piston seizure failure can cause misfires and power loss. On M254 engines, 48V system faults or camshaft centre valve filter defects can cause reduced performance. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C300 petrol badge has represented the V6 and high-performance four-cylinder petrol options across three generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class. From the naturally aspirated 3.0-litre M272 V6 in the W204, through the 3.5-litre M276 V6 in the facelift W204, to the turbocharged 2.0-litre M274 four-cylinder in the W205, and finally the advanced M254 2.0-litre mild hybrid in the W206 - the C300 has consistently offered a compelling blend of power, refinement and efficiency.
